summary.intent: Implement one PR off fresh origin/main that maps NPM_TOKEN and PYPI_TOKEN into the generated matrix workflow's execute job (keeping OIDC working), adds a tokenless trusted-publishing recipe and routing-wording fix to docs/publishing.md, and adds a changeset, for trail #459.
summary.outcome: Tests, template/renderer fix, docs, and changeset were done; just pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, workflow-contracts and ci all passed, mutants caught both mutants, and a signed commit was made. The push, merge of latest origin/main, trail ci-pr, finding resolution and report to the lead were not done in this transcript.

repo: The generated matrix workflow's execute step is built from matrix_workflow.tmpl plus Rust-rendered snippets in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs; the simple workflow goes through callisto-action's run-release.sh, which already maps both tokens.
The rendered matrix workflow bytes are pinned by an insta snapshot (rendered_matrix_workflow_bytes_are_pinned); update with INSTA_UPDATE=always and delete any leftover .snap.new file.
The matrix token-mapping block duplicates run-release.sh logic and had drifted (no leading newline in printf, ignored NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG); AGENTS.md prefers unifying N copies of one logic.
AGENTS.md says the release workflow has no GitHub Environment by owner policy, so docs should not invite environment binding; npm trusted publisher always needs the workflow filename.
The changeset must follow AGENTS.md user-facing style: one idea per bullet, separate **Action:** paragraph, and docs-only corrections may belong in no changeset.
Installed `callisto` binary is older than the repo config, so changesets must be created with `cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add`.
Tests can parse the rendered workflow with yaml_rust2 and run the step's `run` script under bash with a stub `callisto` to assert credentials.
Without NPM_TOKEN, CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG is unset and the publish check runs `npm view` anonymously, which can 404 for restricted packages (earlier E157 timeout in CHANGELOG).

code.finding: MATRIX_NPM_AUTH copied $HOME/.npmrc and used printf '%s\n', drifting from run-release.sh (which honors NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG and prefixes a newline).
Reference implementation of the npm/twine token mapping: copies ${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-$HOME/.npmrc} and appends the token entry with a leading newline.
twine is pinned to ==7.0.0 in the generated workflow.

workflow: The sandbox blocks gpg (~/.gnupg), ~/.npm and uv caches, and network hosts; redirect npm_config_cache and UV_CACHE_DIR to /tmp/claude and run gpg/network gates (workflow-contracts, ci) outside the sandbox.
The shell guard rejects multi-line/compound commands such as heredocs with python and $'...' multi-line args; use Edit/Write tools instead.
Cargo builds cannot run in parallel in one checkout, so run the read-only Opus reviewer while CI runs, and rerun the full gate after applying review fixes.
CARGO_BUILD_JOBS was computed as cores/5 (18 cores gives 3).
Use cargo mutants --in-diff with a diff file written outside the repo and --output outside the repo so mutants.out* is never committed.

friction: Combined heredoc/python shell commands were rejected, forcing the test addition to be redone with edit tools.
The multi-line $'...' changeset summary was rejected by the shell guard; the changeset had to be created with a placeholder and edited.
The installed callisto binary was older than the repo config, requiring cargo run.
just test failed repeatedly in the sandbox (network, ~/.npm and uv cache not writable) until cache dirs were redirected.
workflow-contracts failed in the sandbox because fixture commits needed gpg signing, and had to be run outside it.
The first just ci run was invalidated by review findings and had to be stopped and rerun.
